label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Fernhollow Photo is official!!

Okay, deep breath. I've been sitting on this for weeks and I'm about to explode.

Fernhollow Photo is a real business now. I filed the LLC on October 22. I did it on my lunch break, sitting in my car outside a Fred Meyer, and I cried a little. Okay, more than a little. Then I went back to work and shot an engagement session that afternoon with a perfectly normal face, so nobody knows.

Some of you already know bits of this and some of you are finding out right now, so let me back up.

Rosebud Lane closed at the end of October. Marisol told me on October 6, and I'd shot for her for four years. That's a lot of weddings, a lot of early mornings, and a lot of her coffee, so this is bittersweet in a big way. Marisol basically taught me everything I know about this job. She taught me how to read a room, how to run a timeline without losing my mind, and how to talk a nervous dad off a ledge five minutes before the processional. Whatever kind of photographer I turn out to be, a huge piece of it is hers. Marisol, if you ever read this: thank you. I owe you more cupcakes than I can count.

Here's the part I need you to know. I'm not going to pretend this isn't scary, because it is. But I'm not jumping off a cliff. I've been planning this in my head for two years. I've been saving, learning the business side of things, and figuring out what I'd need before I ever said it out loud. Nothing about this is a whim.

And some of the plan is already working, which is the part that makes me want to dance around my kitchen. I have 14 weddings booked for 2027. Six of those came from Marisol, who sent me every couple she couldn't keep. The other eight found me on their own, which still blows my mind. Busiest month is June with four weddings. The furthest out is a September wedding at Wallowa Lake, which I am already daydreaming about.

My first booking that was 100% mine came in early November. Dahlia and Ken want me for June 12 at Timberline. They found me because of the Multnomah Falls couple photos I'd done. Their email said those photos sold them, and I have read it maybe forty times. Honestly, I'm still not over it.

I also have help for the big days. Jae is my second shooter for the bigger weddings, and I pay per wedding, so Jae's time is covered and I'm not doing everything alone. Having someone next to me who is that good makes the scary parts a lot less scary.

Dad, I know you're reading this, and I know you have Thoughts about health insurance. I have a marketplace plan picked out, and it starts January 1. So you can put your speech away. Mostly. Maybe save it for Christmas.

I also want to explain the name, because a lot of you have asked. Fernhollow is named after the fern hollow trail behind Grandma's old place in Gresham. That's where I took my first real pictures, with her Pentax, and I think about those afternoons every time I hold a camera. Grandma, the name is for you.

When I told Sam, he made a cake for the launch. It said FERNHOLOW. He spelled it wrong. We ate it anyway, every bite, and he has not been allowed to forget it, and he has been doing a very good job of not forgetting it himself.

The website is live, and I'll be sharing more about the work and the couples soon. I'm so grateful for everyone who has looked at my photos over the years and said kind things, even when some of them were blurry.

And since I'll be at Ruthie's in Salem on Thanksgiving anyway, I'm going to bring my camera. If anyone wants free family photos, just say so in the comments or find me by the pie table. Nobody has to be photogenic. Uncle Greg, you can be freezing. I promise to make it look good.

Love you all. Thanks for being my people.

Tessa
